prompt:
A rescue worker walks 300 m north in 240 s and then 400 m east in 360 s.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Vector diagram showing a vertical vector of 300 m pointing North, followed from its tip by a horizontal vector of 400 m pointing East. A dashed resultant arrow R connects the starting point to the final position.]
(a) Draw a vector diagram for the route and label the resultant displacement R. [1]
(b) Calculate the average speed for the complete journey. [2]
(c) Calculate the magnitude of the average velocity. [2]
(d) Determine the direction of the average velocity, measured east of north. [2]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Draw a vector diagram for the route and label the resultant displacement R.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average speed for the complete journey.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the average velocity.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Determine the direction of the average velocity, measured east of north.

marking_points.criterion: Shows 300 m north followed head-to-tail by 400 m east, with R drawn from start to finish.

part_enrichment.guidance: Draw the northward leg first, then the eastward leg starting from its arrowhead. The resultant joins start to finish.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Drawing vectors tail-to-tail or pointing the resultant backwards.

marking_points.criterion: Uses total distance 700 m and total time 600 s.

part_enrichment.guidance: Add both distance components (300 + 400 = 700 m) and both times (240 + 360 = 600 s).
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Using resultant displacement instead of path distance.

part_enrichment.guidance: Use Pythagoras to calculate displacement magnitude R = 500 m, then divide by total time 600 s.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Dividing displacement by the time of only one leg.

part_enrichment.guidance: For an angle east of north, opposite side is East (400 m) and adjacent side is North (300 m).
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Calculating 36.9 degrees (north of east) without specifying the reference direction.

hints: Draw the northward movement first, then begin the eastward movement at its arrowhead.
Average speed uses the entire path length (300 + 400 m) divided by total time (240 + 360 s).
Average velocity uses resultant displacement R = sqrt(300^2 + 400^2) = 500 m divided by total time.
Use tan(theta) = opposite / adjacent = 400 / 300 to find the angle east of north.
solution:
(a) Diagram shows 300 m north, 400 m east head-to-tail, R from start to finish.
(b) Average speed = (300 + 400) / (240 + 360) = 700 / 600 = 1.17 m s^-1.
(c) R = sqrt(300^2 + 400^2) = 500 m. Average velocity = 500 / 600 = 0.833 m s^-1.
(d) tan(theta) = 400 / 300 => theta = 53.1 degrees east of north.
teacher_walkthrough: In part (a), reinforce the head-to-tail vector triangle. The resultant connects the starting point to the final position.
In part (b), emphasize that average speed is scalar: total distance 700 m divided by total time 600 s yields 1.17 m s^-1.
In part (c), calculate resultant displacement R using Pythagoras: sqrt(300^2 + 400^2) = 500 m. Average velocity magnitude is 500 m / 600 s = 0.833 m s^-1.
In part (d), resolve direction: tan(theta) = 400 / 300 gives theta = 53.1 degrees east of north.
